product.amstrad-pc20.summary: The Amstrad version of the compact home PC sold in Britain as the Sinclair PC200.
product.amstrad-pc20.history: Amstrad aimed the PC20 at first-time home PC buyers. For the 1988 Australian Christmas season, the Sunday Times announced A$899 without a monitor and A$1,199 with a colour monitor. In Britain, Amstrad sold the design as the Sinclair PC200.
product.amstrad-pc20.technical.architect: The sources give different clock speeds for the 8086. The Sunday Times announced 8 MHz, while APC reported 10 MHz in its pre-release review.
product.amstrad-pc20.technical.firmware: The shared profile BIOS helps establish the relationship between the two models. Two 8 KiB dumps form a 16 KiB image that identifies itself as Sinclair PC200, the same branding APC saw on its pre-production PC20 at power-on.
product.amstrad-pc20.technical.verified: BluMach includes the shared pc200 profile. The hashes were verified and the BIOS was examined statically.
product.amstrad-pc20.technical.limitatio: A retail PC20 firmware comparison and BluMach boot validation are pending.
